clue.text: Going overseas, say, unknown during affair

indicators.note: during places the unknown inside the affair, as if it happened in the middle of it

parts.note: a fling is a brief romantic affair
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, like X and Z

explanation.surface: Someone heading abroad while an affair is going on, without anyone knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example: travelling overseas by plane is one way of going.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a plane is one example of travelling abroad, hence the 'say' in the clue.

clue.text: Gathering of people united in criminal history

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for united inside the criminal history

parts.note: form is British slang for a criminal record
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: People coming together over a shared criminal past.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a person with 'form' has previous convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is an assembly or meeting place where people gather to discuss matters.

clue.text: Ultimately shady sets of characters around ring primarily — not boxers?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word shady
around puts the typefaces on either side of the letter from ring

parts.note: a font is a complete set of type characters in one design

indicators.note: primarily takes only the opening letter of ring

explanation.surface: A dodgy boxing scene: shady characters gathered around the ring, but they aren't fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are British men's briefs; boxers here are boxer shorts, the rival style of underwear, not fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are close-fitting briefs, the alternative to loose boxer shorts as men's underwear.

clue.text: Chamber group without a website?

definitions.meaning: a chamber ensemble of nine players
read playfully as '...', lacking the internet

explanation.surface: A chamber music group with no online presence.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into NO NET, the internet standing loosely for a web presence.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians playing chamber music together.

clue.text: A job worried someone uncommitted

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
to eat someone is to worry them, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A job that bothered someone with no commitment to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, so is no longer committed to it.

clue.text: Family problem — new chap, for example, not initially fussed about daughter

indicators.note: about wraps the jumbled letters round the abbreviation for daughter
new signals that the following words are to be remade in another order
fussed suggests letters fretted over and thrown into disorder
not initially drops the opening letter of the phrase for example

explanation.surface: A household upset caused by some new man fussing over a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' and 'fussed' both signal the anagram of CHAP plus OREXAMPLE ('for example' without its F); 'about' puts that round D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phaedra complex is a stepmother's desire for her stepson, a named psychological problem within families.

clue.text: Wrong to adopt church line when probing the German war hero

indicators.note: to adopt means the wrongdoing takes the church into itself

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong

indicators.note: probing sends the line into the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A sinful act by the church, with someone investigating the German war hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Oskar Schindler saved over a thousand Jews in the Second World War, so the German connection in the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Oskar Schindler is celebrated for rescuing Jewish workers from the Holocaust, making him a wartime hero.

clue.text: 20th-century style badly rated by company

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters of rated come out wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A twentieth-century design style that a firm has rated poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco was the decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Some instructed, if you instruct

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teacher's self-referential line: some are instructed if you do the instructing.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to improve someone morally or intellectually, which is to teach or instruct them.

clue.text: Aghast — most corn poorly digested — unless you've this?

indicators.note: food poorly digested is churned up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone horrified that most of the corn has gone down badly, unless they have a tough gut.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on the surface: you would be aghast at badly digested corn unless you could stomach it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a tough constitution means you are not easily sickened, so you would not be aghast at this.

clue.text: Holby City character right to back ditching second repeat showing

indicators.note: to back means the hospital worker's letters go in reverse order
ditching means the abbreviation for second is thrown out

parts.note: Holby City was a BBC hospital drama, so a typical character there is a nurse

explanation.surface: A TV drama character backing a repeat broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Holby City was a long-running BBC hospital drama series. Losing S leaves NURE, which 'to back' turns into ERUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast of a programme already shown.

clue.text: Pasta shortcomings rejected by the agitated Italian after reflection

indicators.note: rejected means the shortcomings are turned back on themselves

parts.note: gaps are deficiencies or shortcomings

indicators.note: agitated stirs up the letters of the
after reflection means the abbreviation is seen as in a mirror, backwards

explanation.surface: An agitated Italian, after some thought, dismisses the shortcomings of the pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: Three different signals work on three short pieces: 'rejected' and 'after reflection' both mean turning round, while 'agitated' calls for a jumble; 'by' merely joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a type of long thin pasta.

clue.text: Large creature on stone in sea at Calais

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the French word for sea

parts.note: mer is the French for sea, Calais being a French port
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A huge animal sitting on a rock in the sea off Calais.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight (14 pounds), abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster is any huge or frightening beast.

clue.text: Studies church area in great detail

parts.note: dens are private rooms for study
Ely is a cathedral city and the Isle of Ely is a diocese in eastern England

explanation.surface: Studying the area around a church very thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a familiar crossword source of ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written densely is packed with information, so full of fine detail.

clue.text: Famous ship — alias 'unit at sea'

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A famous ship given an alternative name as a unit at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' is the anagram signal, apt for a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lusitania was the Cunard liner sunk by a German submarine in 1915.

clue.text: Resin shortage not ending

indicators.note: not ending removes the final letter of the synonym for shortage

parts.note: a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A shortage of resin that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is the resinous secretion of an insect, used to make shellac.

clue.text: Fisherman's device — canvas cover set up to carry fish

indicators.note: to carry means the reversed shelter holds the verb inside it
set up in a down clue means the shelter is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fishing device: a canvas cover put up to transport the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns TENT into TNET, which then carries ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle net is a fishing net in which fish become entangled.

clue.text: Where to go and seem only 50% insecure

parts.note: the loo is British slang for the toilet, where one goes

indicators.note: only 50% takes the first half of the word seem

explanation.surface: A toilet that seems only half safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where to go' is a euphemism for the toilet, LOO in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loose is not firmly fixed, so it is insecure.

clue.text: Article overlooked when setting up Hamlet's finale

indicators.note: setting up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
overlooked means the article is left out

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so a Dane
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article left out when staging the end of Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like a play title; it is the man himself, a Dane. Without A it is DNE, which 'setting up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of something is its conclusion, its last part.

clue.text: Nameless writer chasing Catholic clergyman

indicators.note: chasing puts the anonymous writer behind the abbreviation, following it

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, is how an unknown author is credited

explanation.surface: An anonymous author pursuing a Catholic priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral.

clue.text: Spy heading off round Hungary — he hasn't a chance

indicators.note: round sets the shortened word around the abbreviation for Hungary
heading off removes the first letter of the spy's synonym

parts.note: a snooper is someone who spies
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: A spy heading out around Hungary who has no hope of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves NOOPER, which goes 'round' H.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no prospect of succeeding.

clue.text: Estate unhappy about male attached to visiting group

indicators.note: about places the sad word around the other pieces

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: attached to puts the male pronoun on the end of the group

parts.note: a tour is a party of visitors travelling together
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: An unhappy estate, with a man joining a visiting party.
explanation.walkthrough: Stourhead is a famous landscape garden and estate in Wiltshire, owned by the National Trust.
explanation.definitionFit: Stourhead is a country estate with celebrated eighteenth-century gardens in southwest England.

clue.text: Hospital department used cryogenics, perhaps, given encouragement

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
cryogenics freezes things, so one example of using it is to have iced something

explanation.surface: A hospital unit using cryogenic treatment, and being encouraged in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt, so enticed means drawn on or encouraged.

clue.text: Classic play over time getting surprised comment?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
'hello!' can express surprise, as in 'hello, what's this?'

explanation.surface: A classic play running over time, prompting a surprised remark.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Sailor going round China for precious stones

indicators.note: going round means the sailor surrounds the friend

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: A sailor travelling around China in search of gemstones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones, prized as precious stones.

clue.text: Some sailors fixed a disturbed sea when returning

indicators.note: when returning means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: set means fixed, as in a set price
a rip is a stretch of turbulent water

explanation.surface: Sailors who have mended a rough sea on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: SET + A + RIP gives SETARIP, which 'when returning' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are seafarers, though only some sailors are pirates, hence 'Some'.

clue.text: Run business involving one broadcast medium

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: involving means the fuss contains the numeral

parts.note: ado is fuss or business, as in 'much ado'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Running a company that involves a broadcasting outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a medium for broadcasting sound to listeners.

clue.text: What computer key offers — the reverse of upper-case English?

indicators.note: the reverse of means the short form for capitals is written backwards

parts.note: caps is short for capitals, upper-case letters

explanation.surface: A puzzle about keyboards: what does the opposite of upper-case English give?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the reverse of' looks like it asks for lower case; it turns CAPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar on a keyboard puts a blank gap between words.

clue.text: Additional item in program to stop time

parts.note: an app is a software program
to end is to stop
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An extra feature in a piece of software designed to stop time.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added or attached to a larger thing.

clue.text: Daughter positioned at front of a country villa in Russia

indicators.note: positioned at front of moves the daughter's letter to the very start

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa

explanation.surface: A daughter placed in charge of a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: A + CHAD makes ACHAD; its D is moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or holiday cottage.

clue.text: Extendable gag deployed in haunt of vice?

indicators.note: deployed in means the gagging is placed inside the den

parts.note: a sty, figuratively, is a place of filth and depravity; the question mark flags this loose sense
to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A joke told in a den of vice that can be stretched out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' suggests a joke; it is the verb meaning to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic that can be pulled longer is extendable.

clue.text: Food item getting line in no poem

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for line inside the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A food item that finds its way into a poem that isn't one.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a strip of pasta-like dough eaten as food.
